source_policy: Primary California statutory or regulatory source preferred. Secondary guidance and case/decision materials are stored separately from binding authority.

authorities.title: Unprofessional conduct and standard-of-care enforcement
authorities.relevance: Provides the disciplinary framework for gross negligence, repeated negligent acts, incompetence, and related unprofessional conduct.

authorities.title: Prior examination and medical indication
authorities.relevance: Prescribing, dispensing, or furnishing a dangerous drug without an appropriate prior examination and medical indication constitutes unprofessional conduct; the statute expressly permits an appropriate examination through telehealth when the standard of care is satisfied.

authorities.title: Internet prescribing
authorities.relevance: Applies when dangerous drugs or devices are prescribed, dispensed, or furnished on the Internet for delivery to a person in California and requires an appropriate prior examination and medical indication, subject to § 2242.

authorities.title: Prescribing and disciplinary safeguards for controlled substances
authorities.relevance: Preserves Medical Board authority concerning gross negligence, repeated negligence, incompetence, substance-use-disorder treatment, §2242, Internet prescribing, and controlled-substance recordkeeping.

authorities.title: Adequate and accurate patient records
authorities.relevance: Failure to maintain adequate and accurate records relating to patient services for at least seven years after the last date of service constitutes unprofessional conduct.

authorities.title: Telehealth consent and documentation
authorities.relevance: Before delivering health care via telehealth, the initiating provider must inform the patient about telehealth and obtain verbal or written consent; the consent must be documented.
authorities.effective_note: Current statutory text verified 2026-08-15; current version effective January 1, 2026.

authorities.title: Controlled substances: legitimate medical purpose
authorities.relevance: Controlled-substance prescribing must be for a legitimate medical purpose and in the usual course of professional practice, subject to statutory requirements and exceptions.

authorities.title: False or fictitious prescriptions prohibited
authorities.relevance: Prohibits issuing a prescription that is false or fictitious in any respect.

authorities.title: Off-label prescription-drug coverage
authorities.relevance: Limits certain health care service plan exclusions based solely on an FDA-approved drug being prescribed for a different use when statutory conditions are satisfied. The statute includes evidence pathways and assigns the participating prescriber responsibility for supporting documentation when requested.
authorities.important_scope: This is a coverage rule, not a general authorization-to-prescribe rule. It does not apply to Medi-Cal contracts under the Waxman-Duffy Prepaid Health Plan Act.
authorities.effective_note: Current text verified 2026-08-15; amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 136, Sec. 15, effective September 26, 2025.

authorities.title: MTUS Drug Formulary: Off-Label Use
authorities.relevance: Governs off-label drug use within the MTUS Drug Formulary. Prospective review requirements differ depending on whether the drug is Exempt, Non-Exempt, Unlisted, and whether the MTUS Treatment Guidelines recommend the intended off-label use.
authorities.effective_note: Current DWC regulation verified 2026-08-15; operative January 1, 2018.

authorities.title: MTUS Drug List and prospective review
authorities.relevance: Classifies drugs as Exempt, Non-Exempt, or Unlisted and establishes when prospective review is required before dispensing.
authorities.effective_note: Current DWC regulation verified 2026-08-15; operative January 1, 2018.

status_definitions.mandatory: A binding statute or regulation imposes a requirement when its applicability conditions are met.
status_definitions.conditional: A binding authority applies only when specified factual, program, payer, drug, setting, or procedural conditions are present.
status_definitions.advisory: Guidance or recommendations that may inform practice but should not be represented as a binding statutory requirement.
status_definitions.evidentiary: Material that supports or challenges a clinical or factual proposition but does not itself create a legal obligation.
